source_caption:
🎬 Little Man (2006)

Little Man follows Calvin Sims, a small-time criminal with a big attitude who finds himself in a hilarious situation after stealing a valuable diamond. When his plan goes wrong, Calvin disguises himself as a baby to recover the stolen jewel from an unsuspecting couple. Darryl Edwards, believing Calvin is an abandoned infant, brings him home, hoping to start a family with his wife, Vanessa. What follows is a series of outrageous misunderstandings, ridiculous situations, and unforgettable comedic moments as Calvin struggles to maintain his disguise while secretly searching for the diamond. From awkward parenting experiences to chaotic encounters with suspicious family members, every moment becomes more unpredictable. Combining slapstick humor, wild disguises, and the Wayans brothers’ signature comedy, the film delivers a ridiculous adventure filled with laughter and unexpected surprises.

🎭 Genre: Comedy • Crime • Slapstick

⭐ IMDb: 4.5/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 38m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Keenen Ivory Wayans

🏆 Recognition: Starring Marlon Wayans, Shawn Wayans, Kerry Washington, and Tracy Morgan, the film became a recognizable Wayans brothers comedy, known for its exaggerated physical humor, unusual storyline, and outrageous comedic performances.

📺 Where to Watch: Check Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, and Fandango at Home for current streaming, rental, or purchase availability. Availability varies by region.

source_details.synopsis: Little Man is a 2006 American crime comedy film directed by Keenen Ivory Wayans, who co-wrote and co-produced it with Marlon and Shawn Wayans, who both also star in lead roles. The film co-stars Kerry Washington, John Witherspoon, Tracy Morgan, Lochlyn Munro, Chazz Palminteri and Molly Shannon. It follows a jewel thief with dwarfism who hides the proceeds of his latest robbery, then pretends to be a very large baby in order to retrieve it. Theatrically released in the United States on July 14, 2006 by Sony Pictures Releasing, the film was a commercial success, but was critically panned and won three Golden Raspberry Awards.
